items.title: 67520_George Handy oral history interview
items.q: I ran into Jack Segal and explained it to him and we sat down and started writing together. It was very easy to write together, and he and I were knocking things off one after another easily.

ctx.x: I'm so delighted that these things have changed and become acceptable, because I remember the battles I used to go through. I had a period of being a songwriter where I wasn't a musician, a jazz player, a jazz writer and orchestrator, a composer; none of those things, just a songwriter with a lyricist as a partner.
